Project: Kubernetes. Upgrade being assessed: 1.23 -> 1.29.
This change was introduced in release 1.24. Source: Kubernetes v1.24.0 CHANGELOG (official_changelog). Section: v1.24.0 / Changes by Kind / Deprecation.
Version facts from package metadata for this release (authoritative for version numbers): none

ITEM:
<<<
The metadata.clusterName field is deprecated. This field has always been unwritable and always blank, but its presence is confusing, so we will remove it next release. Out of an abundance of caution, this release we have merely changed the name in the go struct to ensure any accidental client uses are found before complete removal.
>>>

PARENT CONTEXT (same section, for disambiguation only):
<<<
v1.24.0 / Changes by Kind / Deprecation: Deprecated Service.Spec.LoadBalancerIP. This field was under-specified and its meaning varies across implementations. As of Kubernetes v1.24, users are encouraged to use implementation-specific annotations when available. This field may be removed in a future API version. Kube-apiserver: the --master-count flag and --endpoint-reconciler-type=master-count reconciler are deprecated in favor of the lease reconciler Kube-apiserver: the insecure address flags --address, --insecure-bind-address, --port and --insecure-port (inert since 1.20) are removed Kubeadm: graduated the UnversionedKubeletConfigMap feature gate to Beta and enabled the feature by default. This implies that 1) for new clusters kubeadm will start using the kube-system/kubelet-config naming scheme for the kubelet ConfigMap and RBAC rules, instead of the legacy kubelet-config-x.yy naming. 2) during upgrade, kubeadm will only write the new scheme ConfigMap and RBAC objects. To disable the feature you can pass UnversionedKubeletConfigMap: false in the kubeadm config for new clusters. For upgrade on existing clusters you can also override the behavior by patching the ClusterConfiguration object in kube-system/kubeadm-config. More details in the associated KEP. Remove tolerate-unready-endpoints annotation in Service deprecated from 1.11, use Service.spec.publishNotReadyAddresses instead. Remove deprecated feature gates ValidateProxyRedirects and StreamingProxyRedirects Remove insecure serving configuration from cloud-provider package, which is consumed by cloud-controller-managers. The --pod-infra-container-image kubelet flag is deprecated and will be removed in future releases The client.authentication.k8s.io/v1alpha1 ExecCredential has been removed. If you are using a client-go credential plugin that relies on the v1alpha1 API please contact the distributor of your plugin for instructions on how to migrate to the v1 API. The node.k8s.io/v1alpha1 RuntimeClass API is no longer served. Use the node.k8s.io/v1 API version, available since v1.20 The cluster addon for dashboard was removed. To install dashboard, see here. The in-tree Azure plugin has been deprecated. The Azure kubelogin plugin serves as an out-of-tree replacement via the kubectl/client-go credential plugin mechanism. Users will now see a warning in the logs regarding this deprecation. The insecure address flags --address and --port in kube-controller-manager have had no effect since v1.20 and are r
>>>

Decide the disposition:
- "risk": the item describes something that can break an app/deployment, require migration work, or create operational risk.
- "context": it is accurate but needs no action at 1.29 (no user action required, deprecated-but-working, additive feature). Give the reason.

For "risk", produce one or more risk paths. Use separate paths for separate symbols/APIs when they can be checked independently. Hard rules:
1. Every condition has at least one quote copied EXACTLY, character for character, from ITEM or PARENT CONTEXT (contiguous span, 3-40 words, no ellipses, no added words). Do not fix typos or formatting.
2. Each path has exactly one condition with category "version" stating that the upgrade crosses release 1.24 (quote the text that ties the change to this release, or the change statement itself), and at least one application/deployment condition (category api_usage, configuration, dependency, runtime, deployment, database, behavior or test_coverage) describing what the app or deployment must use/have for the risk to apply.
3. If the text does not state something you need, do not assert it: use role "uncertain" and explain in ambiguities. derived_by: "extraction" when the text states the fact; for an application/deployment condition ("the application uses X"), use "extraction" when the text names X as the thing affected by the change. Use "inference" only when you infer an affected symbol, scope or impact that the text does not name. Only add ambiguities for real gaps or conflicts in the text, not for the general fact that a specific application has not been inspected.
4. role: "required" (must hold), "alternative" (any one of the alternatives suffices), "optional" (raises impact), "disqualifying" (if it holds, the risk does NOT apply, e.g. not using the new opt-in API), "uncertain".
5. operator/expected_value must be checkable: e.g. operator "present" with expected_value the literal symbol; "less_than" with a version; "equals" with a setting value. expected_value is a string.
6. If a replacement API/setting/version is named, put the migration step in suggested_actions and add a condition for any behavior that differs in the replacement when the text states one.
7. search_queries: for app-side conditions with a literal symbol, give ripgrep regexes (tool "ripgrep"), kubectl commands (tool "kubectl") or SQL (tool "sql") that would find usage. Empty list if no literal symbol.
8. primary_symbol: the most specific identifier of the change (full apiVersion string like "policy/v1beta1", setting name, function, flag, or runtime name like "Python"/"Node.js"). symbols: all identifiers involved.
9. risk_level rubric: critical = upgrade fails or data is at risk for most users meeting the conditions (e.g. unsupported runtime/database version, removed API version that stops serving); high = code or config meeting the conditions breaks at upgrade; medium = behavior change or migration with a clear workaround; low = edge case, cosmetic, or warning-only.
10. fires_at: "upgrade" (at upgrade time), "first_use" (when a feature is first exercised), "rotation" (on credential/password rotation), "rollout" (on deployment rollout), "future_removal" (deprecated now, removed later).
11. applies_to: fill upgrade_method (e.g. "pg_upgrade", "dump/restore"), cluster_type, or from_versions (a version specifier like "<3.1") ONLY if the text restricts applicability; otherwise null.
Do not output confidence.

paths.description: The metadata.clusterName field is deprecated and its Go struct name was changed so that accidental client uses are found before complete removal. Clients that reference this field may be affected.

conditions.statement: The upgrade crosses release 1.24, the release in which the metadata.clusterName change was introduced.
quotes: Out of an abundance of caution, this release we have merely changed the name in the go struct
conditions.relevance: Ties the change to release 1.24, which the 1.23 to 1.29 upgrade crosses.

conditions.statement: The application or deployment uses the metadata.clusterName field or the Go struct field ClusterName.
conditions.relevance: The risk applies only where code or manifests reference metadata.clusterName or the renamed Go struct field.

conditions.statement: The metadata.clusterName field is removed in a later release.
quotes: its presence is confusing, so we will remove it next release
conditions.relevance: The text states the field will be removed in the next release, which affects users who still reference it.
ambiguities: The text does not state whether the field has been removed by Kubernetes 1.29.

suggested_actions: Search manifests, clients and Go code for metadata.clusterName and ClusterName and remove any uses.
Do not rely on metadata.clusterName, since the field is always unwritable and always blank according to the release notes.
